items.title: Advocacy groups sue AI giants to freeze new models, warning of 'catastrophic' risks
items.excerpt: A coalition of online safety and consumer advocacy groups has sued five leading AI companies in a California state court, asking it to halt further development of advanced AI systems they say pose 'imminent and catastrophic risks'.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.excerpt: Rep. Bill Foster, a cosponsor of the Chip Security Act, says Nvidia told him the bill's location-verification anti-smuggling measures are technically feasible, even as an industry group called them 'potentially infeasible'; the bill is getting renewed attention after Jensen Huang's resignation.

items.title: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
items.excerpt: Axios reports, citing sources, that President Trump approved action to curb Nvidia chip flows to China three times, but Commerce Secretary Lutnick stalled the export-control step each time.

items.title: Scoop: Inside Bessent's Situation Room confrontation with Lutnick over China chip security
items.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Bessent and Commerce Secretary Lutnick clashed in the Situation Room over a suspected diversion of Nvidia chips to China via Megaspeed, according to Axios sources.

items.title: "미, 중국 AI 칩 '동남아 우회로' 차단 추진" — 싱가포르·말레이시아 등 7개국 수출허가 대상
items.excerpt: The Information 보도에 따르면 미 상무부 BIS가 중국 기업의 제3국 데이터센터 경유 원격 AI 칩 사용을 막기 위해 싱가포르·말레이시아·태국·인도네시아·브라질·노르웨이·남아공 7개국에 블랙웰급 이상 칩 수출허가 의무를 적용하는 규정을 마무리 중이며, 이르면 이달 발표될 수 있다. (보도 기반, 규정 미공표)

items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
items.excerpt: Nvidia's cofounder and CEO resigned after the company opened an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset — a national-security scandal now driving chip-export-control bills in Congress. (Exec-move framing; keep only if the curator treats the export-control/espionage angle as the hook.)

items.title: United Kingdom-Norway Joint Statement of intent on Artificial Intelligence
items.excerpt: Primary document: the UK and Norway sign a joint statement of intent to deepen AI cooperation, covering compute, defence, AI security and international governance.

items.title: France to open international defence AI centre in 2027
items.excerpt: Paris plans to open an international defence AI centre in 2027 and seek NATO accreditation for it once revised rules allow it. (Article page Cloudflare-gated; time from outlet RSS.)

items.title: Photoshop maker Adobe backs rules against AI style mimicry
items.excerpt: Adobe is pitching EU lawmakers on rules giving artists recourse against commercial AI style copycats. (Article page Cloudflare-gated; time from outlet RSS.)

items.title: EU needs only 'very trusted partners' on AI chips, tech chief says amid Nvidia crisis
items.excerpt: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen says Europe should source AI chips only from 'very trusted partners' and keep business secrets in Europe, as the Nvidia espionage scandal unfolds.

items.title: EU watchdog probes Commission's AI pick over conflict of interest concerns
items.excerpt: The European Ombudsman opened an inquiry and will inspect Commission documents over the appointment of Jim Hagemann Snabe as EU AI envoy.

items.title: Political campaigns spent $187 million promoting AI-generated ads in the 2026 midterms. Did they work?
items.excerpt: Campaigns spent $187M promoting AI-generated political ads in the 2026 midterms; deepfakes and AI-enhanced imagery became commonplace while campaigns stayed wary of voter backlash and misleading content.

items.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
items.excerpt: Families in seven US cities protested Google's Gemini pilot on school Chromebooks and called for AI moratoriums in schools, after a teen's lawsuit labeled Gemini a 'suicide coach'.

items.title: NHS England deletes 'misleading' claim 137 trusts benefiting from Palantir AI tools
items.excerpt: NHS England removed its claim that 137 trusts benefit from Palantir's Federated Data Platform after the Guardian found 29 trusts were not or barely using it.

items.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
items.excerpt: As US governments adopt AI, public-sector unions are winning contract language and state/local safeguards on how AI is used and against job displacement.

items.title: AI has made it 'close to impossible' to assess university coursework, regulator says
items.excerpt: England's Office for Students says generative AI makes coursework nearly impossible to assess and urges institutions to return to traditional exams and in-person presentations.

items.title: Friends of the Court Flock to the OpenAI Copyright Fight
items.excerpt: A roundup of the amicus briefs filed in the OpenAI copyright-infringement litigation, with resources for tracking the legal arguments on AI training and fair use.

items.title: Inside Greece's new AI Act framework
items.excerpt: Greece's new national AI Act implementation framework distributes regulatory oversight across authorities, supports innovation and strengthens enforcement and transparency requirements. (Member analysis.)

items.title: Yahoo is the first to sign up for new pay-to-scrape collective AI licensing
items.excerpt: Yahoo becomes the first signatory of the Internet Licensing Collective (formerly RSL), a standard requiring AI companies to pay for scraping via a collective license rather than one-off deals.

items.title: Data center critics are gearing up to hold politicians to their campaign promises
items.excerpt: Groups that pushed data center restrictions plan to hold newly elected officials to their promises after voters backed limits in all but one ballot measure. (Follow-up to covered ballot-measure story; low novelty.)

items.title: 한-유엔 군축·비확산회의 서울서 개최…AI의 군사적 영향 논의
items.excerpt: 외교부 주최 '한-유엔 군축·비확산회의'가 12~13일 서울에서 열려 AI의 군사적 영향 등을 논의한다 (CCW 검토회의 11-16 앞둔 회의).

items.title: 中 AI 기업들, 젠슨 황 스캔들 속 해외서 엔비디아 칩 용량 확보 분주...美 규제 강화 우려
items.excerpt: 로이터 보도 인용: 중국 AI 기업들이 미국의 원격 칩 사용 규제 강화를 우려해 해외 데이터센터의 엔비디아 칩 기반 컴퓨팅 용량 확보에 나섰다.

items.title: Police investigate 219 cases involving election deepfakes, misinformation
items.excerpt: Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau has investigated 219 election-related misinformation and deepfake cases ahead of the November vote, referring 176 people in 134 cases to prosecutors. (Off-list exception: no on-list outlet covered this enforcement action.)

items.title: Kenya's AI Bill 2026: Key Things to Know After Rejection By Senate ICT Committee
items.excerpt: Kenya's first dedicated AI bill has stalled after the Senate ICT Committee recommended its rejection. (Off-list exception: legislative action not covered by on-list outlets.)
